text:
Noah: FYI — Customer Acme (case #5421) on Private VPC. They report control-plane audit logs missing for 10:31-10:42 UTC and users seeing intermittent 403s when we call their KMS-wrapped key. Repro and logs below, tagging infra + security.

Noah: Repro steps from the customer:
1) Deploy model in private VPC (subnet: 10.2.0.0/24)
2) Call Redwood control plane endpoint via our VPC egress proxy
3) ~5% of requests to /v1/keys/... return 403, other calls succeed.

Noah: Example request they captured (redacted):
```
curl -v -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.ai/v1/keys/decrypt \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\
  -d '{"ciphertext":"..."}'
* Connected to controlplane.redwood.ai (34.12.45.67) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/keys/decrypt HTTP/1.1
> Host: controlplane.redwood.ai
> ...
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"kms:access_denied"}
```

Noah: They also ran tcpdump on the customer side, showing TLS handshake then short RSTs (~same timing as 403s). They attached a pcap but pasted a short excerpt: 
```
10:31:12.123456 IP 10.2.0.5.52344 > 34.12.45.67.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
10:31:12.124321 IP 34.12.45.67.443 > 10.2.0.5.52344: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
10:31:12.125000 IP 10.2.0.5.52344 > 34.12.45.67.443: Flags [.], ack 1
10:31:12.130000 IP 34.12.45.67.443 > 10.2.0.5.52344: Flags [R], seq 1, ack 1
```

eli: Thanks — a few quick checks we need from the customer:
- Do they NAT through a NATGW or egress via proxy? (we've seen proxy header stripping break KMS auth)
- Security group egress open to 34.12.45.67:443 (and/or control plane CIDR)?
- Any HTTP proxy (squid/mitm) that might strip SNI or Authorization headers?

maria: Also need retention/forwarding details for their audit logs. Are they shipping logs to a SIEM? If logs are missing on our side, we should confirm whether control-plane received the request at all — check our ingress LB logs for the timestamps (10:31-10:42 UTC).

jenna: Quick infra notes:
- If they're using a NATGW with route table misconfig, TCP can reset if return path incorrect.
- MTU/DF issues sometimes cause TLS weirdness on some on-prem setups.
- If a proxy is terminating TLS and re-establishing upstream, ensure it forwards TLS SNI (or use CONNECT tunnel).

Noah: Customer answered: they use a corporate proxy in the VPC (transparent) + NATGW fallback. They said SG egress was open but proxy env var set on containers. They pushed pcap and said the proxy sometimes sends RSTs.

eli: Okay — that points at the proxy. Two things to validate on their side:
1) Capture `curl -v --proxy <proxy> https://controlplane.redwood.ai/v1/health` from a host that reproduces the 403 and paste headers.
2) Check proxy logs around 10:31 for any `HTTP/1.1 403` or `403 Forbidden` responses from upstream.

maria: From compliance perspective, also confirm: are they truncating or redacting Authorization headers before forwarding logs to their SIEM? If audit logs we receive are missing fields we may think entries are absent. Need full ingestion pipeline check.

jenna: Suggested workaround while we triage: have customer bypass the proxy (route NATGW directly) for a canary subnet and see if 403s disappear. If that fixes it, proxy is the culprit.

Noah: I've asked customer to repro with proxy bypass and to run `iptables -L -n` and `cat /etc/hosts` (they have custom DNS). Also asked them to share exact proxy vendor/version.

support-bot: Case link: https://support.redwood.ai/cases/5421 — escalated to eng-infra + security.

eli: If customer confirms proxy is the issue, next steps:
- eng-infra to provide recommended proxy config for KMS/control-plane (CONNECT + pass-through SNI + do not strip Authorization)
- security to document data-retention/ingest checks so we can prove whether control-plane saw requests
- set up a live repro session with customer and capture server-side LB access logs + pcap on both ends

maria: Assigning owner: @jenna to coordinate live repro (please set time). I'll prepare an incident evidence checklist (timestamps, LB logs, proxy logs, pcaps, request IDs).

Noah: Thanks all — customer will try bypassing proxy in ~30m and report back. Will paste results here.

Noah: (30m later) Customer confirmed bypass removed 403s and audit entries reappeared in our control plane for the missing window. They will keep proxy vendor logs and we will work on recommended config.

maria: Closing triage: root cause likely transparent proxy altering TLS/headers leading to KMS auth failures and missing audit ingestion. Follow-ups: eng-infra to publish proxy guidance and we should add a runbook entry for Private VPC proxy traps.

eli: I'll open a PR with proxy config examples and add tests to our Private VPC quickstart.

jenna: Scheduling a 1hr sync with customer and eng-infra Monday to finalize config and get logs for SOC review.

Noah: Marking case updated. :white_check_mark:
